title: Counting Second-Order Schreier Sets with Minimum 2
authors: Dongho Kim
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17371v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A finite nonempty set $X \subset \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ is (first-order) Schreier if $|X| \leq \min X$. These Schreier sets can be generalized recursively to higher-order Schreier sets, and we specifically investigate the second-order Schreier sets. We show that the count of second-order Schreier sets with minimum element $2$ and maximum element $n+4$ is one more than the $n^\text{th}$ term of the convolution of the Fibonacci numbers $F_1, F_2, \ldots$ with $F_2, F_3, \ldots$ (given by Sequence A023610 in the OEIS).

title: Erratum to Power boundedness and related properties for weighted composition operators on $\mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$, Journal of Functional Analysis 288 (2025), 110745
authors: Vicente Asensio, Enrique Jord\'a, Thomas Kalmes
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17382v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As was kindly pointed out to us by S. Li, the proofs of Theorem 2.11 and Lemma 3.1 in our original paper contain errors that require modifications of the corresponding statements. We also correct a gap in the proof of Lemma 2.1, whose statement remains valid. Furthermore, we explain the consequences for several subsequent results and provide the necessary corrections to their statements and proofs.

title: Composition operators on weighted Beurling--Sobolev spaces
authors: St\'ephane Charpentier (I2M), Rachid Zarouf (ADEF)
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17392v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Given a function $\varphi:\D\to \D$ holomorphic in a neighborhood of the closed unit disk $\overline{\D}$, we study the matrix \[ A_\varphi = \big(\widehat{\varphi^n}(k)\big)_{n,k\geq 0}. \] We obtain a complete characterization of those $\varphi$ for which $A_\varphi$ acts boundedly from $\ell^p$ to $\ell^q$, $p,q\in [1,\infty]$. These results can be reformulated in terms of composition operators, providing a complete description of the symbols $\varphi$ holomorphic in a neighbourhood of $\overline{\D}$ that induce a bounded composition operator $C_\varphi:f\mapsto f\circ \varphi$ between two possibly different Beurling--Sobolev spaces. In particular, we prove that $C_\varphi$ is bounded on $\ell_a^p$ for some $p\neq 2$ if and only if it is bounded on every $\ell_a^p$, $p\in [1,\infty]$, if and only if $\varphi$ satisfies an analytic condition at the points of $\overline{\D}$ where it touches the unit circle. Extensions to weighted Beurling--Sobolev spaces are also provided.

title: A Cut Finite Element Method with Boundary Value Correction for Robin, Neumann and Interface Conditions
authors: Erik Burman, Peter Hansbo, Mats G. Larson
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17445v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We extend the cut finite element method with boundary value correction of Burman, Hansbo and Larson [Math.\ Comp.\ 87 (2018) 633--657] to Robin and Neumann conditions and to interface problems with imperfect bonding. The formulation retains a piecewise affine boundary for all integration, while using the exact geometry only at boundary quadrature points.
  The correction uses Taylor expansions of the solution and its gradient along the discrete normal, with the exact normal used to evaluate the transported flux. At an interface, a further correction to the normal flux jump accounts for the difference between these two normals. Under the stated trace and Poincar\'e bounds, the corrected form is an $O(h^{1/2})$ perturbation of a symmetric form, whose matrix can therefore be used as a preconditioner.
  For a fixed finite Robin coefficient, we obtain the energy error bound $C_\beta(h^p+\delta_h^{m+1})$, whereas the bound uniform in the Robin coefficient is $C(h^p+h^{-1/2}\delta_h^{m+1})$, provided the Poincar\'e constant is uniform. With $\delta_h=O(h^2)$, the sufficient Taylor orders are therefore $2m+2\ge p$ and $2m+\frac32\ge p$, respectively. Numerical examples for $p=1,2,3$ illustrate these rates and the effect of the flux-jump correction in the interface problem.

title: Distributionally Robust Risk Evaluation with Low-Rank Perturbations
authors: Linglingzhi Zhu, Dongze Wu, Yao Xie
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17447v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study distributionally robust risk under perturbations restricted to low-rank matrices whose row and column spaces are shared across observations, focusing on how much worst-case risk this restriction sacrifices and how to compute the restricted worst case. Under moment or Wasserstein budgets, we derive quantitative bounds on the gap between the unrestricted and low-rank worst-case risks, characterize when the gap vanishes, and identify the smallest lossless row and column dimensions. To generate worst-case perturbations, we apply projected gradient ascent to a curvature-corrected concave problem and derive computable risk certificates. We establish global sublinear convergence for the corrected objective and linear convergence to a worst-case distribution when the budget constraint is sufficiently active.

title: Ozone groups and fixed rings of double Ore extensions
authors: Andr\'es Rubiano
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17476v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We determine centers of two families of four-dimensional double Ore extensions without torsion assumptions, restricting to $f\ne0$ in $\mathcal O$. On the PI locus of $\mathcal K$, we classify the ozone groups and obtain normal commutative fixed rings of generic degree two over the center, including a nonmonogenic example. For an odd-torsion subfamily of $\mathcal O$, independent odd orders $n\geq1,m>1$ yield ozone group $C_n^2\times C_2^2$, PI degree $2nm$ and fixed-algebra PI degree $m$, with unchanged center. A PI specialization of $\mathcal G$ has trivial ozone group.

title: First-order characterizations of strong quasiconvexity with the exact modulus
authors: John Matos Ascona, Jackeline C. Huaccha Neyra, Lizet Santa Cruz Calder\'on, Heraclio L\'opez-L\'azaro
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17477v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we study first-order characterizations of strong quasiconvexity for functions defined on convex subsets of real normed spaces. For functions that are continuous along segments, an inequality involving the lower Dini derivative is a known necessary condition for strong quasiconvexity with a given modulus, whereas the established converse guarantees only half of that modulus. By means of a one-dimensional lemma, we prove that this inequality, and even its weaker version with the upper Dini derivative, ensures strong quasiconvexity with the same modulus, without requiring the domain to be open; this answers a question raised in the recent literature. The main result leads to a characterization with the same modulus in terms of the Clarke subdifferential for locally Lipschitz functions on Banach spaces, which answers another open question, and to a formula for the exact modulus of radial functions defined on Hilbert spaces. We also present some consequences in optimization, such as an optimality condition without Clarke regularity, an error bound with optimal constant and, for the projected subgradient method, the same convergence rate as in the strongly convex case, together with the exponential convergence of the associated flow. Finally, we show that the converse of a relation between proximal points and strong subdifferentials fails in general, but holds for a truncation of the function.

title: Quantum Fundamental Groups of Spaces with Finite-Sheeted Universal Covers
authors: Shuzhou Wang, Zhenhua Wang, Matthew Zediker
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17485v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Discrete quantum groups have attracted much interest, but there was a lack of natural examples until Voigt constructed quantum permutations of finite and infinite sets in arXiv:2208.01310. In this paper, we construct the quantum fundamental groups that contain the classical fundamental groups as subgroups. This is a new class of natural examples of discrete quantum groups arising from symmetries of covering spaces in topology. We characterize quantum fundamental groups for a wide class of examples, including $\mathbb{RP}^2$. We show that these quantum fundamental groups are genuinely quantum for spaces with finite fundamental groups that are either non-abelian or of non prime order.

title: Convergence Properties of PF-Exec: Homogeneous Structure, Anchored Closed Form, and Gain Dynamics
authors: Hanzhang Jia, Liheng Zeng, Yiran Li, Yi Gao, Bo Ma
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17488v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper establishes a layered mathematical char acterisation of PF-Exec, the algorithm of the companion system paper. Demand-proportional bandwidth allocation yields an exact first-order homogeneous decomposition, from which the equal-load bandwidth target and its feasibility bound follow in closed form. The logarithmic knee view preserves strict load order and shares its global optimum with the Jain fairness index, while the demand-weighted centroid minimises the position potential. The damped softmax association block possesses a fixed point on the product of simplices. The truncated one-dimensional gain iteration admits a complete characterisation, with geomet ric convergence below the critical gain, initial-value-dependent bounded oscillation at it, and a family of bounded two-state cycles above it. A global invariant error ball and an explicit tracking recursion complete the execution guarantee. A numerical audit confirms the structural identities on every measured state and quantifies the local amplification of the coupled association and resource dynamics. Together, the results explain how closed form recovery directions and bounded adaptive gains provide stable execution without requiring a global Euclidean contraction assumption.

title: Noncommutative Rational Positivstellens\"atze with Operator Coefficients
authors: Abhay Jindal, Igor Klep, Jurij Vol\v{c}i\v{c}
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17493v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We establish a convex Positivstellensatz for noncommutative rational functions with bounded operator coefficients. A hermitian operator-valued rational function that is positive semidefinite on a matrix convex set described by a linear pencil admits a positivity certificate consisting of rational hermitian squares and a completely positive term involving the defining linear pencil. The certificate comes with an explicit complexity bound independent of the dimension of the coefficient Hilbert space. As a consequence, we solve the operator-valued noncommutative rational analog of Hilbert's 17th problem: every positive semidefinite operator-valued noncommutative rational function is a sum of hermitian squares, and even a single hermitian square when the coefficient Hilbert space is infinite-dimensional. In contrast, the corresponding commutative statement fails for infinite-dimensional operator coefficients.

title: Correlation distribution for a class of Niho exponents via self-conjugate-reciprocal polynomials and Kloosterman sums
authors: Yongbo Xia, Chunlei Li, Xiangyong Zeng, Tor Helleseth
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17506v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $q=2^m$ for an even $m\geq 6$ and let $d=s(q-1)+1$ with $4s\equiv5\pmod{q+1}$. In this paper, the correlation distribution between a binary m-sequence of period $q^2-1$ and its $d$-decimation is considered. The cross-correlation function takes seven values $q(i-1)-1$ for $0\leq i\leq 6$, and we determine their frequencies based on the study of low-degree self-conjugate-reciprocal polynomials and three mixed Kloosterman sums, which are finally expressed in terms of $K_m(1)$ and $K_m(\omega)$, where $K_m(\cdot)$ is the Kloomsterman sum on the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ and $\omega$ is a primitive element of $\mathbb{F}_4$.

title: Cartan Dynamics and Limit Sets on Flag Manifolds
authors: \'Angel Cano, Marlon M. L\'opez-Flores, Jos\'e Seade, Andrew Shaw
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17510v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The classical convergence principle describes the collapse of the Riemann sphere under divergent sequences of M\"obius transformations. We develop its counterpart for arbitrary real semisimple Lie groups acting on flag manifolds, and use it to study limit sets and domains of discontinuity of discrete subgroups. The key is to let the source move: the destination of $x$ under $(g_m)$ is the set of all limits of $g_mx_m$ with $x_m\to x$. Our destination formula computes it as the closure of a unipotent orbit, determined by the Cartan data and a bounded Levi factor. The stratified convergence principle organises these destinations into families of translated Schubert varieties attached to boundary points of a compactification of the group. Over the complex numbers, the destination relation is the support of Brion's limiting graphs in the wonderful compactification, providing scheme structures, multidegrees and diagonal intersections.
  For discrete groups, the union of destination relations determines proper discontinuity and whether a largest domain exists. It relates Quint's flag limit set, Conze--Guivarc'h, Kulkarni and Myrberg sets to the recurrent set, while balanced choices of cells yield domains for every discrete subgroup, without Anosov hypotheses. For symmetric-power actions of non-elementary Kleinian groups on $\mathbb{CP}^N$, we compute the largest domain by a multiplicity bound at points of the classical limit set; for $N\ge3$ it strictly contains the Kulkarni domain, which equals the equicontinuity region. We also obtain nonempty largest domains for Zariski-dense cusped Hitchin groups with unipotent elements, and examples of strongly irreducible groups with no largest domain.

title: Gusto: a toolkit for compatible finite element dynamical cores
authors: Jemma Shipton, Thomas M. Bendall, Colin J. Cotter, David M. Acreman, Timothy C. Andrews, Jack Betteridge, Alex Brown, Thomas H. Gibson, Nell Hartney, David A. Ham, Joshua Hope-Collins, Jeremy A. Pike, Connor J. Ward, Dan Witt
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17540v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Gusto is a tool for rapid prototyping of new algorithms based on compatible finite element methods for discretising the fluid equations in the dynamical core of weather and climate models. In this context, the development of new algorithms typically follows a path that involves testing on a hierarchy of simpler equation sets sharing important features of the mathematical structure of the equation set solved by the dynamical core. Gusto provides compatible finite element spatial discretisations of the hierarchy of equation sets, along with a range of timestepping schemes. The code is modular so that different spatial and temporal discretisations can be combined and the same schemes can be applied to any of the equation sets. This facilitates fair comparison of the schemes and makes the extension of any algorithmic developments to the more complex equation sets more straightforward. In this paper we present Gusto to the community by describing the algorithms implemented in Gusto and showcasing their performance through a variety of test problems commonly used in numerical weather prediction.

title: Innovative Integrated Congestion Management Market: Synergizing Operational Flexibility of Transmission System Operators with Aggregator-Driven Resources
authors: Arash Beiranvand
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17613v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper introduces an innovative congestion management market that seeks to integrate and harness the operational flexibility available to Transmission System Operators (TSO) in conjunction with the flexibility offered by aggregators. In the context of operational flexibility, this study investigates Network Topology Optimization (NTO) as a pivotal strategy for to address the transmission network congestion, specifically through the strategic switching of certain buses. To achieve this, an N-1 secured NTO is formulated using a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) methodology. Concurrently, acknowledging the crucial and growing importance of aggregator-provided flexibility in congestion management, the paper presents a novel integrated congestion management market. In this framework, aggregators submit bids, and the TSO, taking into account these bids alongside the potential for the NTO, clears the market with the goal of minimizing the overall cost of congestion management. The proposed integrated market is constructed using a linear optimization model, ensuring its practical applicability in real world scenarios. The effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed market design are assessed using the standard IEEE 39-bus system, with results indicating promising potential and applicability

title: Complete Center Classification of a Quintic $\mathbb Z_2$-Equivariant System via Rational Descent and Ramification
authors: Feng Li, Meilan Cai, Chaochao Sun
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17633v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a new structural method to completely classify the elementary centers of a ten-parameter quintic $\mathbb Z_2$-equivariant system. The method overcomes the computational bottleneck of direct focus-quantity elimination by combining a Li\'enard reduction, a necessary-and-sufficient analytic involution criterion, and rational descent with residue and ramification analysis. We obtain forty-two explicit original-parameter conditions covering the entire center locus, including all degenerate and boundary cases. Sufficiency is established constructively through integrating factors, first integrals and explicit reversible realizations.

title: Optimal Dividend Problem for a Threshold Dependent Surplus Process with Bounded Dividend Rate
authors: Zhongqin Gao, Panyu Wu, Xiaowen Zhou
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17656v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study optimal bounded-rate dividend payments for a diffusion surplus process whose drift and volatility change at a fixed surplus threshold. Optimal strategies admit an exhaustive classification into zero-threshold, positive single-threshold, two-boundary, and three-boundary configurations. The latter two configurations have separated dividend regions, which arise because the interface can reverse the monotonicity of the derivative of the value function with respect to the initial surplus. Multiband optimality requires an upward change in drift. Without prescribing a strategy in advance, we construct the unique bounded classical solution of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman transmission problem by varying the derivative at zero surplus and selecting the unique value for which the resulting solution agrees in both value and derivative with a bounded solution at a fixed sufficiently large surplus level. Verification identifies this solution with the value function and determines the optimal feedback strategy. For each configuration, we derive necessary and sufficient optimality conditions and characterize the switching boundaries through explicit formulas or equations in one unknown obtained by matching the value function and its derivative. The analysis also shows how changes in the drift and volatility of the upper regime affect the optimal value and dividend strategy. Numerical analysis illustrates how model parameters affect the optimal dividend regions.

title: Agent-written heuristics versus commercial solvers on unsolved job-shop benchmark instances
authors: Andre Albrecht, Enzo Morosini Frazzon, Leandro C. Coelho, Bruno Vieira
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17682v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Commercial solvers are the standard tool for difficult scheduling problems. We study whether a frontier large language model, used as a coding agent with open-source tools only, can match them in quality and speed. We report every run, and independent checkers verify every schedule. On the 100,000-operation job shop tai_100_1000_1, an agent-written solver reached 525,515, below OptalCP, Hexaly, and CP Optimizer. Unchanged, it improved all ten instances of the family and closed two. With equal budgets on the same workstation, it ended 0.0-1.8% above the lower bound, against 2.6-5.8% for CP Optimizer and 2.4-4.4% for Hexaly. On the Behnke-Geiger flexible job shops, an agent-written tabu search improved 11 of 32 open instances. With two transport robots, an agent-written solver improved seven of ten MKT instances. New lower bounds show that four published MKT values cannot be attained on the distributed instance files. Agent-run improvement campaigns closed eight further instances.

title: A Unified Framework for First- and Second-Order Energy-Stable Parametric Finite Element Methods for Planar Willmore Flow
authors: Xiaoli Li, Yujing Yan
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17700v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The construction of structure-preserving schemes for planar Willmore flow that are second-order accurate in time and avoid large coupled nonlinear solves remains challenging. In this work, we develop a unified framework for first- and second-order fully discrete energy-stable parametric finite element schemes for planar Willmore flow with a length-penalization term. The framework is based on a new equivalent reformulation involving a global auxiliary variable. The main novelty lies in the second-order construction, which combines midpoint curvature quantities weighted by elementwise arc-length Jacobian ratios with a compatible discrete tangent to obtain exact discrete chain rules for the bending energy and curve length. A further contribution is to show that both schemes satisfy discrete modified energy dissipation laws that yield the same type of a priori bounds on the discrete solution as the original energy law. They also retain Barrett--Garcke--N{\"u}rnberg tangential motion to promote favorable mesh distribution. Each stage reduces to two linear solves with exactly the same coefficient matrix and one scalar nonlinear solve. We rigorously prove unique solvability of the linear subproblems under suitable assumptions and derive computable sufficient conditions for local existence and uniqueness of the scalar solution near unity. Numerical experiments demonstrate the expected temporal accuracy, energy dissipation, good mesh quality and computational efficiency.

title: Online Carbon-Aware Power Flexibility Quantification of Distributed Data Centers
authors: Xiaowei Wang, Yue Chen
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17714v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Geographically distributed data centers (DCs) can provide spatio-temporal power flexibility to electric grids through the coordinated management of computing resources and energy. Beyond their energy consumption, the carbon footprints of DCs are non-negligible, which constrain the power flexibility that DCs can offer to the power grid. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a carbon-aware power flexibility quantification framework for DCs. We first develop an optimization model that characterizes DC power flexibility in a grid-usable form, namely the Cartesian product of adjustable power demand intervals across time slots. An online algorithm based on Lyapunov optimization is then designed to solve the flexibility quantification model in real time under uncertain workload arrivals and fluctuating grid carbon intensity. Furthermore, an integrated disaggregation and feedback mechanism is devised to translate the power system operator's dispatch commands into real-time DC operating decisions and to capture their impact on future DC flexibility. Several desirable properties of the proposed model and method are proven, including disaggregation feasibility, bounded workload processing delays, and a bounded suboptimality gap. Numerical simulations demonstrate that our approach effectively unlocks DC power flexibility while satisfying carbon emission constraints, outperforming baseline algorithms.

title: Proximal Adam algorithm for nonsmooth composite optimization and linear convergence under proximal PL geometry
authors: Xiaopeng Zhu, Zhongyi Huang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17727v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We analyze Adam-type methods for nonsmooth composite optimization problems $\min_x\Phi(x)=f(x)+h(x)$, where $f$ is smooth and $h$ is convex, proper, and lower semicontinuous. The nonsmooth term is treated by a metric-weighted proximal map, while the smooth term is preconditioned by the Adam second-moment matrix. We prove a composite descent lemma whose constants depend explicitly on the spectral bounds of the adaptive metric and a residual--step equivalence that converts proximal step decay into subgradient stationarity. These yield an $O(1/N)$ bound on the minimum proximal stationarity residual for the deterministic proximal normalized gradient method without convexity of $f$, and the same $O(1/N)$ rate for proximal Adam under quantitative momentum-alignment and residual-coherence conditions together with a metric-compatibility condition. By estimating the momentum error directly, the same $O(1/N)$ rate is also obtained without the momentum-alignment and residual-coherence assumptions. When the composite objective satisfies a proximal Polyak--{\L}ojasiewicz inequality, both algorithms and the relaxed proximal Adam scheme converge linearly with explicit contraction factors. Numerical experiments on a diagonal Lasso problem, two-dimensional image TV denoising, and two-dimensional elastic parameter identification illustrate the predicted stationarity and linear rates.

title: Rigidity for pivotal braided r-categories of moderate growth and applications to vertex operator algebras
authors: Robert McRae
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17732v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an abelian pivotal braided r-category with simple unit object $\mathbf{1}$ over any field. We present a ChatGPT-generated proof, prompted by Bin Gui, that any object $X$ in $\mathcal{C}$ of moderate growth, in the sense that $\dim\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, where $D$ is the Grothendieck-Verdier duality functor of $\mathcal{C}$. Using this variant, we show that if $V$ is a simple self-contragredient vertex operator algebra such that the category $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ of $C_1$-cofinite grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is closed under contragredient modules, then $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ is a locally finite $\mathbb{C}$-linear abelian rigid braided ribbon category. We also show that if $V$ is a simple $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$-graded self-contragredient $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra, then the category of all grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is a (not necessarily semisimple) modular tensor category.

title: High-probability convergence of adaptive, proximal, and clipped Adam-type methods for nonconvex stochastic optimization
authors: Xiaopeng Zhu, Zhongyi Huang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17736v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper develops a unified high-probability analysis of adaptive, proximal, and clipped first-order methods for nonconvex stochastic optimization. For a smooth objective whose stochastic gradient error has sub-Gaussian norm, the normalized adaptive gradient method attains the standard stochastic nonconvex complexity of the square root of the number of iterations, with an additional logarithmic dependence on the inverse confidence level that is inversely proportional to the number of iterations. The proof uses an adaptive descent decomposition together with Freedman and Bernstein concentration inequalities. The same guarantee is established for the full adaptive moment method under an explicit momentum-alignment condition. The analysis is extended to projected and proximal updates through a stationarity measure based on the subdifferential distance, to objectives satisfying the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition, and to heavy-tailed noise through truncation. The framework is applied to stochastic inverse problems in elasticity, and numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical scaling and the practical behavior of the methods.

title: Minimaxity in Robust Nonparametric Regression: from Heavy-Tailed to Sub-Gaussian Assumptions
authors: Yikun Li, Matey Neykov
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17744v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study nonparametric regression over star-shaped function classes under strong adversarial contamination. The clean (original) observations $(\tilde{X} _{i},\tilde{Y} _{i})_{i=1} ^{n}$ are i.i.d. and satisfy $\tilde{Y} _{i}=f ^{*}(\tilde{X} _{i})+\xi _{i}$, where $f ^{*}\in \mathcal{F}$, $\tilde{X}$ is distributed as $\mathbb{P} _{X}$, and the noise is conditionally centered. An adversary may inspect the clean sample and replace at most $\lfloor \epsilon n\rfloor$ observation pairs. We assume that $\mathcal{F}\subset L _{2}(\mathbb{P} _{X})$ is star-shaped with finite diameter $d$.
  Under a Bernstein-type moment condition on function increments and a bounded conditional second moment for the noise, we establish the matching lower and upper bounds of order $\left((\eta ^{*}) ^{2} \vee \epsilon \right)\wedge d ^{2}$, uniformly over admissible star-shaped function classes, therefore characterizing the minimax rate of estimation error, where \begin{equation*}
  \eta ^{*}:=\sup\left\{\eta >0: n\eta^2\leq\log \mathcal M _{\mathcal{F}}^{\text{loc}}(\eta,c)\right\}. \end{equation*} Here $\log \mathcal{M} _{\mathcal{F}} ^{\text{loc}}(\eta,c)$ denotes the local metric entropy of $\mathcal{F}$ in $L _2(\mathbb{P} _{X})$, and $c$ is a sufficiently large constant. Under a uniform relative sub-Gaussian condition on function increments and noise, the lower bound is adjusted to $\left((\eta ^{*})^{2}\vee \epsilon ^{2}\right)\wedge d ^{2}$ while the upper bound improves to $\left((\eta ^{*})^{2}\vee \epsilon ^{2}\log ^{2}\left(\frac{e}{\epsilon }\right)\right)\wedge d ^{2}$, yielding minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors.

title: The Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz Paper: A 10-Year Retrospective
authors: Hamed Karimi, Julie Nutini, Mark Schmidt
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17745v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In 2016, we wrote a paper introducing the phrase "Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition" for an old idea, unsure of how readers would react. The paper ultimately had a larger impact than we expected, and we are surprised and honoured to receive the 2026 PKDD ECML Test of Time Award. With 10 years of hindsight, this note offers an informal and candid retrospective on the PL condition. We take a look back at the origins of the paper, give an AI-assisted refined version of the main theorem, review criticisms of the work, and discuss a variety of related ideas and extensions.

title: Convergence analysis of physics-informed neural networks for subdiffusion
authors: Bangti Jin, Qiqi Rao, Zhi Zhou
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17759v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks have emerged as mesh-free solvers for partial differential equations, yet their rigorous convergence theory for time-fractional problems remains limited. We present a convergence analysis of PINNs for linear subdiffusion equations and for the associated backward problem of recovering the initial data from terminal observations. To address the nonlocality and weakly singular kernels of fractional derivatives, we introduce a discretization-based PINN framework built on some popular time-stepping schemes satisfying discrete maximal regularity, including backward Euler, BDF2, L1, and fractional CN schemes. This approach avoids the exact evaluation of fractional derivatives at training points while preserving the stability structure needed for convergence analysis. For the forward problem, we prove that, under the natural fractional maximal-regularity condition $u\in W^{\alpha,p}(0,T;L^2(\Omega))\cap L^p(0,T;H^2(\Omega)\cap H_0^1(\Omega))$, the piecewise linear temporal reconstructions of PINN-loss minimizers converge to the exact solution. This result avoids the higher-order regularity assumptions on the exact solution that are often imposed in existing PINN convergence analyses. We also verify the required discrete maximal regularity and consistency properties for the aforementioned popular time discretizations. We then extend the analysis to the backward subdiffusion problem and establish convergence of the regularized recovery of the initial data from terminal observations, despite its ill-posedness. Numerical experiments for both forward and backward problems support the theoretical results, demonstrate the necessity of regularization, and show that $L^2$-type losses alone are generally insufficient. These results establish a rigorous theoretical basis for discretization-based PINNs for time-fractional diffusion problems.

title: Toward the Minimal Set of Information Inequalities in Regenerating Codes: An Algebraic Approach
authors: Rui-Juan Jing, Laigang Guo, Yan-Feng Xie, Chun-Ming Yuan
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17765v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Information-theoretic outer bounds for exact-repair regenerating codes can be formulated as linear programs, but the associated Shannon-type systems contain many implicit equalities and redundant inequalities. We directly specify a reduced system for the $(n,n-1,n-1)$ exact-repair model using the closure structure induced by its repair dependencies. Nonempty closed sets index the reduced joint-entropy coordinates, and inseparable edges determine the defining inequalities. We prove equivalence with the initial system by characterizing its implicit equalities and establishing sufficient redundancy criteria. We also give an algorithm that constructs the directly defined system for any $n$, count its entropy coordinates, and derive an explicitly computable upper bound on its number of inequalities. For every $n\ge2$, we prove that the reduced system has no implicit equalities and that each distinct defining inequality is nonredundant and defines a facet in the nonempty closed-set coordinate space. Exact enumerations for $n\in\{2,3,4,5\}$ verify the reported system sizes.

title: Compatible by Construction: Bottom-Up Nonlinear Model Reduction without Interface Bases
authors: Youngkyu Kim, Youngsoo Choi
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17773v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Nonlinear manifolds can provide compact representations of solutions to partial differential equations (PDEs), but generating training data and learning these representations on large domains remain costly. We present a bottom-up framework that reuses local nonlinear representations learned on a small training domain to solve larger PDE systems. A shared nonlinear decoder represents the full set of degrees of freedom owned by each subdomain, without separate interior and interface models. Each global degree of freedom has a unique owner, and local residuals directly use decoded state values from the corresponding neighboring subdomains. The resulting discrete state is single-valued by construction, eliminating the need for independent interface copies and additional interface compatibility constraints. Physical coupling is retained through the original time-discrete PDE residual. With the decoder held fixed, the subdomain-specific reduced coordinates are determined jointly by minimizing this residual, and the Gauss--Newton system is assembled from local contributions. Experiments on parameterized viscous Burgers and incompressible Navier--Stokes problems demonstrate reuse on larger domains without retraining. Comparisons with local proper orthogonal decomposition models under the same coupling construction show favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-offs in the tested regimes.

title: Localization for Lipschitz monotone quasi-periodic operators with power-law hopping
authors: Hongyi Cao, Yunfeng Shi, Peizhen Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17799v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove spectral and dynamical localization for quasi-periodic operators on $\mathbb Z^d$ with Lipschitz monotone potentials and power-law hopping. For sufficiently small coupling, localization holds at every allowed phase whenever the hopping decay exponent $r$ exceeds the Diophantine exponent $\tau$. The proof is based on multiscale analysis with exponentially growing scales. We use homotopy in the coupling constant to select the local eigenvalue branches and Schur complement estimates to control the successive elimination of coordinates.

title: An accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping
authors: Wen Jiang, Hao Luo
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17813v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we propose an accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping for unconstrained convex multiobjective optimization problems in a real Hilbert space. The continuous flow is formulated as a system of two first-order equations involving only a single multiobjective projection operator and suitable time-scaling factors. Formally, it can also be expressed as a second-order system with explicit multiobjective Hessian-driven damping, which corresponds to the usual Hessian-driven damping introduced by Alvarez et al. [J. Math. Pures Appl., 81(8):747--779, 2002]. The first-order formulation, however, involves no Hessian term and can be regarded as an extension of the Hessian-driven Nesterov accelerated gradient flow by Chen and Luo [arXiv:1912.09276, 2019]. Assuming that the objective gradients are Lipschitz continuous on bounded sets and that the common lower level sets are bounded, we establish global existence in finite dimensions under suitable time-scaling conditions. An a priori energy estimate confines the solutions to a fixed bounded set, and a Lyapunov argument yields fast decay of a merit function and the KKT residual. Under an additional bound on the time-scaling factors, the trajectory of every global solution converges weakly to a weak Pareto point. Numerical tests illustrate the rapid residual decay and reduced oscillations.

title: High-Dimensional Gaussian and Bootstrap Approximation: Near $1/\sqrt{n}$ Rates with General Covariance
authors: Miles E. Lopes, Ricardo Masini
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17923v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider Berry-Esseen bounds over rectangles for sums of $n$ random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^p$ that are i.i.d. A longstanding open question in high-dimensional probability and statistics is whether bounds of order $1/\sqrt n$ are attainable up to factors of $\log(pn)$ when the population covariance matrix is unrestricted. We answer this question affirmatively, provided that the random vectors have sub-Gaussian entries with non-zero variance. In addition, we provide analogous results for bootstrap approximation and Gaussian comparison, which make use of a special discrepancy measure between covariance matrices that enables improvement with respect to prior work. Taking an approach based on interpolation, the novel aspects of the proofs deal with bounding the interpolation derivatives in a way that is not sensitive to the covariance structure.

title: Statistical guarantees for signature kernel ridge regression
authors: Christian Bayer, Jakob Kellermann
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17934v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Path signatures are a standard tool for learning functionals on path space. The main underpinnings of their application are universal approximation results. For a wide range of function classes on path space, these results state that any function in such a class can be approximated arbitrarily well by a linear functional of the path signature. Hence, linear functionals of the signature are in principle expressive enough for learning functions on path space. Nonetheless, these results do not provide insights into the statistical question of how much data is needed to identify a suitable signature functional. In this work, we study this question in the framework of kernel ridge regression with the signature kernel. The target is the conditional expectation $\E[Y|X]$, where $X$ is the observed path and $Y$ is a real-valued response. Under different assumptions on the moments of the signature kernel and the response, we provide finite-sample and consistency guarantees for the method. We supplement our theoretical analysis with numerical experiments that illustrate our results.

title: A narrow band method for non-causal discretizations of anisotropic eikonal equations, with adaptive width, sub-and super-solution construction, and quasi-linear complexity
authors: Jean-Marie Mirebeau (CNRS, CB), Yanis Mouheb (CB, CEA/DAM)
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17947v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We describe a narrow band method for numerically solving anisotropic eikonal equations, and more generally static first order Hamilton-Jacobi equations with possibly non-convex Hamiltonians, discretized using standard schemes (semi-Lagrangian, upwind-differences, Lax-Friedrichs). The causality property is not needed, in contrast with the fast marching method. The proposed approach simultaneously builds a numerical sub-solution u and super-solution u to the problem, and adapts the width of the narrow band based on their comparison. We prove that (1 + $\epsilon$)u $\ge$ u at termination, where $\epsilon$ > 0 is any given tolerance parameter, and that the worst case complexity is O(N | ln $\epsilon$| ln(N/$\epsilon$)), where N denotes the number of discretization points, and the underlying constant is explicit in terms of those associated with the scheme properties. Numerical experiments illustrate our results.

title: Auto-conditioned Gradient Descent Methods for Multiobjective Optimization
authors: Shuaichenji Jiang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17949v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper proposes two linesearch-free algorithms based on steepest descent methods for smooth multiobjective optimization: auto-conditioned steepest descent method for multiobjective optimization (AC-SDM) and auto-conditioned normalized gradient descent method for multiobjective optimization (AC-NGDM). Both algorithms estimate the local Lipschitz constant from the function values and the first-order information obtained in previous iterations. AC-SDM uses a shared estimate of the Lipschitz constant to construct a scaled steepest descent direction. For AC-NGDM, we use each function's local Lipschitz estimate to normalize the gradient of the corresponding function and construct the descent direction. We prove that every accumulation point of any sequence generated by both algorithms is a Pareto critical point. We also establish convergence rates of $O(1/\sqrt{k})$ for nonconvex objectives and $O(1/k)$ for convex objectives. Numerical results on several test problems demonstrate that AC-SDM and AC-NGDM require fewer iterations and less CPU time than the multiobjective steepest descent method with an Armijo line search and a max-type nonmonotone line search.

title: Wireless Node Ranking via Fourier-Driven Maximum-Likelihood Estimation (extended version)
authors: Daniel Schneider, Hannes Frey
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17973v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We apply non-abelian Fourier theory to the problem of maximum-likelihood estimation of the order of a line topology, based on signal strength measurements under shadowing only. This yields up to a 60-fold speedup over standard methods for uncorrelated shadowing.
  Moreover, for correlated Gaussian shadowing with a singular covariance (e.g. the joint path-loss model), maximum-likelihood recovery is exact and independent of the shadowing variance (an infinite Le Cam threshold), which our implementation confirms for $\sigma/\alpha$ as high as 7.0. The key object is the covariance's null space. Its dimension is fixed by the topology; its orientation depends on the correlation function only through the per-link variances.
  Although the mechanism formally requires an exact line, it is robust to small perturbations of the formation: an approximate kernel recovers as well as the exact one. We explore the dependence on the perturbation in detail for five nodes.

title: The Train Unit Shunting Problem with Service Scheduling and Workforce Assignment: classical and quantum optimization approaches
authors: Alessia Ciacco, Francesca Guerriero, Eneko Osaba
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17987v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Efficient railway rolling stock management requires the coordinated planning of train-unit assignment, shunting movements, track occupation, service operations, and workforce allocation. These interdependent decisions give rise to a challenging combinatorial optimization problem, particularly as the size of the fleet and the planning horizon increase. This paper introduces the Train Unit Shunting Problem with Service Scheduling and Workforce Assignment, a mixed-integer linear programming formulation that integrates these operational decisions within a unified optimization framework. To improve computational tractability, a preprocessing procedure is developed to reduce the size of the resulting model. The proposed approach is evaluated through computational experiments on instances of increasing size and under different objective-function weight and cost configurations. Classical optimization experiments using Gurobi show that filtering method reduces the number of decision variables and constraints, while its impact on computational time varies across instances. In addition, a constrained quadratic model representation is investigated using D-Wave's hybrid quantum-classical optimization solver.

title: A Realizability-Based Kinetic-Fluid Domain Decomposition Method for Single-Temperature Gas Mixtures
authors: Domenico Caparello, Lorenzo Pareschi, Thomas Rey
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18068v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper introduces a domain-adaptive numerical method for multi-species kinetic models that relax toward a single-temperature and single-velocity hydrodynamic limit. To this end, we derive moment realizability matrices for this regime. In this way the ideas of Levermore, Morokoff, and Nadiga are extended to non-equilibrium mixtures in which inter-species and intra-species collisions occur at comparable rates, so that all species relax to a common velocity and a common temperature. The realizability conditions are used as an indicator to divide the computational domain, at each time step, into macroscopic and kinetic regions. In the kinetic regions, where the continuum description fails (e.g., across strong shocks, non-equilibrium interfaces, or kinetic boundary layers), the method solves the multi-species kinetic equations. Close to local thermodynamic equilibrium, the Euler equations of the mixture are solved instead. Confining the kinetic computations to the non-equilibrium regions reduces the simulation time, while the results remain close to those of the full kinetic solver. The method is discretized on Cartesian grids with high-order schemes in space and time. The kinetic equations are integrated with an Asymptotic-Preserving Implicit-Explicit (IMEX) scheme, so that a consistent discretization of the single-velocity, single-temperature Euler system of the mixture is recovered when the Knudsen number goes to zero. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first realizability-based adaptive spatial domain decomposition method for gas mixtures in this single-velocity, single-temperature setting.

title: High-order IMEX local discontinuous Galerkin methods with sparse grids for high-dimensional nonlinear parabolic PDEs
authors: Joel P. Villarino, Manuel J. Castro, J. A. Garc\'ia-Rodr\'iguez, J. G. L\'opez-Salas
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18079v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this work, we develop a high-order IMEX-LDG scheme on sparse grids for solving nonlinear parabolic PDEs in moderate to high dimensions. The method combines the advantages of LDG methods for convection--diffusion problems, IMEX-RK time integrators for stiff systems, and sparse-grid techniques to mitigate the curse of dimensionality. The resulting scheme is fully parallelized in MPI, is robust, efficient, and scalable, making it suitable for a wide range of applications involving high-dimensional nonlinear parabolic PDEs.

title: On the convergence of the False Nearest Neighbours algorithm
authors: Adam \'Spiewak
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18087v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The False Nearest Neighbours (FNN) algorithm is one of the most widely used methods for choosing the embedding dimension, i.e. the number $k$ of delay coordinates, in the time-delay reconstruction of a dynamical system from an observed scalar time series. We prove rigorous results on the behaviour of this algorithm for long time series. We consider a smooth dynamical system on a compact manifold $M$ and an invariant probability measure $\mu$. For a typical measurement function and $\mu$-almost every trajectory, we show that the proportion of false nearest neighbours tends to zero (provided that the tolerance threshold is large enough) once $k >\dim M$. On the other hand, for systems with super-polynomial decay of correlations, we prove that this proportion tends to one whenever $k$ is smaller than the Hausdorff dimension of $\mu$. Consequently, in this case, the FNN algorithm (run for long enough time series) returns an embedding dimension $k$ satisfying $\dim_H \mu \leq k \leq \dim M + 1$. This is below the threshold $2\dim M + 1$ required by the Takens embedding theorem, so the classical Takens embedding theory does not explain why reconstructions and predictions with $k$ chosen by the FNN algorithm work in practice. The explanation for this case is provided by a recent probabilistic theory of time-delay embeddings. We apply our results to the H\'enon and Lorenz attractors, showing that the FNN algorithm typically returns $k=2$ for the H\'enon map (in the chaotic case) and $k \leq 3$ for the Lorenz system.

title: Bound-preserving finite volume scheme for a coupled parabolic system with nonlinear and nonlocal drift
authors: Nicklas J\"averg{\aa}rd, Adrian Muntean
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18090v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a bound preserving finite-volume scheme for a coupled system of partial differential equations with nonlinear, nonlocal drift. The main contribution of this work is twofold: $(1)$ we show that the proposed scheme preserves physically motivated bounds; $(2)$ we prove that the scheme is well-posed and leads to a sequence of approximate solutions converging to the weak solution of the original problem. This setting is motivated by questions related to morphology formation in organic solar cells.

title: Singularly embedded solitons and Stokes phenomenon in the fifth order KdV equation
authors: Roberto Barrio, Vassili Gelfreich, J. Tom\'as L\'azaro, Juan Ramon Pacha
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18102v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study embedded solitons (ES) in a fifth-order Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation near a reversible Hamiltonian saddle-centre bifurcation. The solitons correspond to homoclinic orbits to an equilibrium whose linearisation has a pair of real and a pair of purely imaginary eigenvalues. Existence of symmetric homoclinic near the bifurcation is a codimension-one phenomenon governed by a parameter-dependent Stokes constant associated with an inner equation. Using complex matching, we derive an oscillatory large-parameter asymptotic formula for the Stokes constant. This formula implies the existence of a countable sequence of zeros and gives their asymptotic distribution in parameter space. We also develop two complementary high-precision numerical procedures for evaluating the Stokes constant: one based on the late terms of the formal inner expansion and another on direct computation of the stable and unstable manifolds. The numerical results agree with each other and with the asymptotic prediction, confirming both the existence and the predicted locations of the embedded-soliton branches.

title: Muon Attains $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ Iteration Complexity under Shuffling
authors: Kun Huang, Shi Pu, Karl Henrik Johansson
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18124v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Muon is a stochastic first-order optimizer for matrix-valued parameters. It maintains an exponential moving average of stochastic gradients in a momentum buffer with coefficient $\beta$, and orthogonalizes the buffer to obtain the update direction. Muon has been reported to accelerate and stabilize the training of large language models. In practice, it is often used with shuffling (sampling without replacement), where each epoch visits the components of a finite-sum objective in a permuted order. However, its iteration complexity in this setting remains open. We analyze Muon under shuffling, with the momentum buffer orthogonalized by the polar map. For smooth nonconvex finite-sum problems, we establish an $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ iteration complexity for finding an $\varepsilon$-stationary point. This guarantee holds for every sequence of permutations, covering random reshuffling, shuffle once, and the incremental gradient method. This complexity matches that of stochastic gradient descent under shuffling in its dependence on $\varepsilon$, and improves on Muon's $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-4})$ complexity under sampling with replacement. Our guarantee requires a problem-dependent $\beta$ that approaches one as the number of components grows. In contrast, no fixed $\beta$ guarantees convergence to stationarity for every number of components. We show this by constructing a family of smooth convex problems on which, for any fixed $\beta\in[0,1)$, Muon remains bounded away from stationarity once the number of components is sufficiently large. This failure occurs for every sequence of permutations and persists even with small stepsizes. These results suggest two practical tuning rules: if the training loss stops decreasing even after reducing the stepsize, increase $\beta$; when increasing $\beta$, reduce the stepsize accordingly.

title: Rate Optimal Streaming Codes Under an Extended Delay Profile for Three-Node Relay Networks
authors: Ke Wang, Wenjie Ma, Zhipeng Li, Yaqiang Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18137v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study streaming codes for a three-node relay network with burst lengths $b_1,b_2$ and an end-to-end decoding delay $T$. Let $u=\max\{b_1,b_2\}$ and $v=\min\{b_1,b_2\}$, and write $T-v=pu+q$, where $T\ge u+v$ and $0\le q<u><v$. Second, for equal burst lengths $b$, it attains the bound if and only if $b\mid(T-2b)$; a quantitative upper bound gives a strictly positive rate gap in every nondivisible case. These converses allow nonlinear components and predetermined time variation within the stated ordinary-forwarding architecture. Existing adaptive schemes for equal bursts approach the same rate upper bound asymptotically using time-varying convolutional codes and lie outside the non-adaptive setting considered here.

title: Characterizing M-estimators using canonical divergences from information geometry
authors: Paul Navas
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18141v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: On Euclidean space, the losses that produce consistent M-estimators of a functional are its strictly consistent scoring functions (Dimitriadis, Fissler and Ziegel, 2024), and Osband's principle characterizes these through identification functions, which define method-of-moments estimators. We extend this characterization to the probability simplex. We define the residual, which on Euclidean space is a subtraction, as the inverse exponential map of an affine connection. It identifies the exponential barycenter of the connection: the arithmetic, normalized geometric and Fr\'echet means for the mixture, exponential and Levi-Civita connections. Its integral along geodesics is the canonical divergence of Ay and Amari (2015). A geometric form of Osband's principle decides which losses each connection admits. For the flat connections every strictly convex generator yields a consistent Bregman loss. For the curved $\alpha$-connections, half the squared Fisher-Rao distance is (up to scale) the only consistent loss for the Fr\'echet mean, and for $\alpha \notin \{-1, 0, 1\}$ no such loss exists and only the method of moments remains. The residual is integrable only at $\alpha = 0$, sharpening the integrability claim of Ay and Amari. The characterization yields the estimating equations of regression on the simplex and the calibration decomposition of compositional forecasts.

title: Hamming and Johnson-Type Bounds for Joint Error Correction and Detection
authors: Yulin Chen, Raymond W. Yeung
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18156v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We derive upper bounds on the size of codes for joint error correction and detection over classical $q$-ary Hamming spaces. A $(c,c')$ joint error correcting and detecting code corrects every error of weight at most $c$ and detects every error whose weight lies between $c+1$ and $c+c'$. We establish equivalent conditions for this decoding requirement using Hamming balls and Hamming rings, and derive a joint bound that reduces to the Hamming bound when $c'=0$. We introduce joint perfect codes and show that binary repetition codes attain the joint bound whenever $n=2c+c'+1$. For codes satisfying $d_{\min}=2c+c'+1$, we investigate an alternative joint bound based on ring multiplicity and constant-weight code bounds. A further argument using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and pairwise ring intersections yields a refined joint bound that is always at least as strong as the original joint bound. We then incorporate an additional outer Hamming shell to obtain a Johnson-type extension. This extension provides a strict improvement for binary codes with $c'=1$, $d_{\min}=2c+2$, $c\geq2$, and $d_{\min}+2\leq n\leq3d_{\min}/2-1$. These results connect sphere-packing bounds with the geometry of joint error correction and detection.

title: An entropy-stable splitting strategy for a hyperbolic dispersive shallow-water model on unstructured meshes
authors: Fr\'ed\'eric Couderc, Arnaud Duran, Maria Kazakova, Bastien Lombard, Pascal Noble, R\'emy Baraille, Jean-Paul Vila
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18166v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper presents an entropy-stable splitting strategy for the numerical solution of a hyperbolic approximation of the Serre--Green--Naghdi (SGN) model, leading to an efficient solver for dispersive water waves on unstructured meshes. The model was introduced by Escalante et al. (2019) and justified shortly thereafter by Richard (2021) as an asymptotic model of the free-surface Euler equations under a weak compressibility assumption. While the parent model includes full topography terms and enhanced dispersive properties, the present study focuses on its mild-slope form without enhanced dispersion, which retains an exact energy equation, the cornerstone of the stability analysis. The splitting yields a shallow-water subsystem with two passive scalars, governed by the \textit{slow} gravity waves, and an acoustic subsystem carrying the dispersive effects, governed by the \textit{fast} acoustic waves. The gravity step adapts an existing entropy-stable scheme, while an original scheme is derived for the acoustic step; both dissipate the energy at the discrete level, under local fully discrete stability criteria on general unstructured meshes. Complementary linear analyses select the low-dissipation calibration of the gravity step used in the computations, outside the scope of the nonlinear estimate. The acoustic step, which requires no global linear solve, is sub-iterated after each gravity time step; the resulting solver is three to six times more expensive than a classical shallow-water solver, depending on the chosen acoustic speed. Numerical validations, ranging from academic benchmarks to a realistic coastal configuration, highlight the properties of the approach and pave the way for operational use.

title: Safety Certificates for Systems under Attack via Stackelberg Set Games
authors: Nikolaos Athanasopoulos, David Laverty, Gregory Provan, Quanyan Zhu
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18173v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study a Stackelberg set selection game for linear systems subject to bounded disturbances and additive attacks. The defender selects the vector parameter of a polytopic safe set template; the attacker, after observing this choice, selects the vector parameter of an admissible attack set. The payoff is a signed, facet-normalised invariance margin that tests invariance exactly and quantifies either the available contraction or the facet inflation needed when invariance fails. Both controlled and robust controlled invariance are treated, corresponding to different information patterns for the control input. Exploiting the structure of parameterised polyhedra, we show that within each validity region the margin is concave in the attack parameter, which reduces the follower minimisation to finitely many extreme parameters. The complete max--min game is then solved by a finite family of LPs, one per defender validity region, each enforcing all attacker regions under a common defender decision and guaranteed margin. The framework handles hard state constraints and additional costs related to the safe set size, and recovers optimal set parameters together with state and attack realisations that activate the certificate. A load frequency control example under false data injection illustrates the construction, the validity decomposition, and the two information patterns.

title: Sample complexity and scalability of adaptive-sampling trust-region methods for zeroth-order stochastic optimization --- Part~II: a new pathwise analysis with randomized subspaces
authors: Sara Shashaani, Coralia Cartis, Kwassi Joseph Dzahini
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18174v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Stochastic trust-region methods are usually analyzed in expectation or with high probability: the guarantee is about the law of the algorithm, not about the run in hand. This paper analyzes the adaptive sampling stochastic trust-region method ASTRO-DF (which is the reuse variant ASTRA-R in Part I) in random subspaces along almost every sample path. The route has one probabilistic ingredient, the accuracy of the common-random-number estimates at the adaptive sample size, uniformly over the trust region; Part~I established it by chaining, here it is obtained at the stopping time by optional stopping and converted, by the first Borel--Cantelli lemma, into an accuracy that holds from a random index on, after which the deterministic trust-region argument applies. We prove almost sure convergence and almost sure iteration and sample complexity of orders $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(d\epsilon^{-2})$ and $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(d^2\epsilon^{-4})$, with a subspace dimension growing logarithmically; we show that at a fixed subspace dimension the eventual-accuracy argument yields $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\epsilon^{-2-\mathcal{O}(1/p)})$ iterations and $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\epsilon^{-4-\mathcal{O}(1/p)})$ samples; we show that the random index after which the rates hold cannot be too large and has an explicit, rapidly decaying tail. Compared with the supermartingale route, the pathwise route needs no lower bound on the per-iteration probability of a good iteration, no coupling between the trust-region expansion factor and the sketch, and no moment condition on the summed squared radii.

title: Movable Antenna-Aided ISAC: A Time- and Frequency-Division Framework
authors: Yuyan Zhou, Haocheng Hua, Jie Xu, Rui Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18196v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper investigates movable-antenna (MA)-enhanced integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) under time division duplex (TDD) and frequency division duplex (FDD) protocols, where sensing and communications occupy orthogonal time and frequency resources, respectively. A wideband target-position Cram\'er-Rao bound (CRB) is derived under a pulse-radar framework with pulse compression, incorporating delay and angle estimation error bounds in Cartesian coordinates. Both bounds depend on sensing power; the delay bound also depends on sensing bandwidth, while the angle bound depends on the effective aperture determined by the antenna position vector (APV). A worst-case position CRB over a prescribed target region ensures robust sensing performance. For multiuser downlink communication, joint APV and resource-allocation problems are formulated for TDD and FDD to maximize the minimum achievable user rate subject to the sensing requirement. An alternating optimization algorithm is developed for FDD, while TDD is addressed by searching over feasible sensing pulse numbers combined with APV optimization. Representative scenarios clarify how MA improves channel orthogonality and enlarges the sensing aperture, and how these effects shape the TDD/FDD rate comparison. Numerical results show that APV optimization enlarges the communication-sensing tradeoff region over fixed-position antenna benchmarks. The optimized configurations exhibit distinct tendencies: TDD favors a larger antenna position variance, whereas FDD favors better channel orthogonality among users.

title: Consensus-Based Optimization of Path-Integral Free Energy for Model Predictive Control
authors: Daisuke Inoue, Yuyang Huang, Dante Kalise
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18208v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose CBO-MPPI, a sampling-based predictive controller that applies consensus-based optimization (CBO) to the free energy underlying model predictive path integral control (MPPI). Under hard constraints, this objective rewards sampling neighborhoods containing feasible, low-cost trajectories under perturbation. Standard MPPI performs a local stochastic search by updating one nominal control sequence from Gaussian perturbations around it. In CBO-MPPI, we estimate the free energy at multiple nominal centers from local rollouts. These estimates define a shared consensus that guides drift and diffusion, and the final selected center supplies an MPPI weighted-mean output. For the associated mean-field model, we establish well-posedness and, under additional assumptions, convergence toward a free-energy minimizer. In simulations of obstacle navigation, pendulum swing-up, and planar-arm manipulation under equal rollout budgets, at high temperatures, CBO-MPPI attains lower free energy than MPPI and multi-start MPPI and maintains greater obstacle clearance than CBO-MPC.

title: Causal and conditional tail coefficients: asymptotics, inference and graph recovery
authors: Axel B\"ucher, Mario Krali
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18225v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The causal tail coefficient (CTC) measures the influence of an extreme value of one variable on another variable and has been proposed as a tool for causal discovery in heavy-tailed models. Despite its popularity, the asymptotic behavior of its empirical counterpart has not been well understood. We develop an asymptotic theory for the rank-based CTC estimator with an intermediate threshold under nonparametric conditions that are satisfied by all standard copula models. A key observation is that the CTC is determined by the mean of a conditional tail limit distribution, which clarifies its interpretation and determines the asymptotic variance of the estimator. We establish joint asymptotic normality for the entire CTC matrix and prove consistency of a multiplier bootstrap for simultaneous inference. For heavy-tailed linear and recursive max-linear structural equation models, we show that the CTC equals one if and only if the first variable is an ancestor of the second, which leads to confidence graphs for the ancestral graph with asymptotic coverage guarantees. All results extend to general conditional tail coefficients, defined as further functionals of the conditional tail limit distribution. A simulation study and an application to dietary intake data illustrate the methods.
